issues.legal_issue: The compensation fixed for acquired land with substantial development potential is not excessive where comparable plot sales are adjusted for their small size and developed setting.
material_facts: The acquired land was fertile, irrigated, level agricultural land and was acquired for expansion of an industrial focal point.
The acquired land was close to an area already developed as an urban estate, and the High Court found it had high potential for industrial or similar development.

A sale of a small plot in a developed colony before the acquisition notification was used as a comparable, with a substantial deduction made to account for the plot’s small size and developed setting.
The State challenged the compensation fixed by the High Court as excessive.
issues.conclusion: The compensation fixed by the High Court was not excessive, and there was no warrant to interfere with it; the State’s appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Compensation may be assessed by considering the land’s potentiality and comparable sale transactions, while adjusting for material differences such as the small size of a plot and its location in a developed colony. The Court treated the High Court’s assessment as cogent and convincing. The judgment cites no earlier cases; it refers to the acquisition notification under section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act as the relevant acquisition context.

predicates.state_appeal_against_land_compensation_a: The acquiring State appealed against a court’s award of compensation for acquired land.
predicates.land_has_development_potential: The acquired land was near developed property or was otherwise suitable for the development purpose underlying the acquisition.
predicates.comparable_plot_sale_adjusted_for_size_a: A sale of a small plot in a developed area was used as a comparison, with an adjustment for those differences.

issues.definition: When the State appeals a land-compensation award and the land has development potential or a comparable plot sale is adjusted for size and development, the compensation award is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant receiving compensation for acquired land is entitled to the applicable statutory benefits under the amended compensation provisions.
material_facts: The case concerned compensation for land acquired under the Land Acquisition Act.
The Court expressly stated that the claimant was entitled to the statutory benefits under the amended provisions concerning additional compensation, solatium, and interest.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to the statutory benefits under sections 23(1A), 23(2), and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied sections 23(1A), 23(2), and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, which provide the applicable statutory benefits in addition to compensation. The judgment cites no earlier cases on this issue.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.amended_statutory_benefit_requirements_a: The amended legal requirements provide statutory benefits in addition to compensation for the acquired land.

issues.definition: In an appeal concerning land-acquisition compensation, when amended statutory benefit requirements apply, the claimant is entitled to the applicable statutory benefits.

issues.legal_issue: Compensation and associated statutory benefits that remain unpaid after prolonged proceedings must be paid within the time directed by the Court.
material_facts: The land had been acquired many years before the appeals were finally decided.
The appeals had remained pending for an extended period, and the Court stated that the delay was not attributable to any party.
The Court directed the acquiring government to pay the compensation and other benefits within a specified time.
issues.conclusion: The government was directed to pay the compensation and other benefits within the time fixed by the Court.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the prolonged delay in payment and the fact that the delay was not attributable to any party in directing prompt payment. The judgment cites no statutory provision or earlier case for this direction.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning compensation for acquired land.
predicates.compensation_remains_unpaid: The acquiring government has not yet paid the compensation or associated benefits due for the acquired land.
predicates.appeal_delay_not_attributable_to_any_par: The proceedings have been delayed, and the delay is not attributable to any party.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerning land-acquisition compensation involves unpaid compensation and delay not attributable to any party, the government must pay the compensation and benefits promptly.
